say: A storm has locked the night shift inside the Helix research facility, with up to fourteen others. Some of them... aren't human anymore. And nobody knows who.
Everyone gets a secret role. Most players are human. One to three start infected. Zombies can see each other. Humans can't see anyone.
Walk up to anyone and challenge them. They have five seconds. Accept, and you both walk to a duel table. Or run.
Run, and the challenger gets eight seconds to catch you. Get touched, and the duel is forced. Ladders are your friend.
There are only four kinds of card. Number cards, one to nine. Higher number wins, and the winner takes the loser's card.
The Zombie card. Only zombies hold it. It beats any number, even a nine, and the loser turns into a zombie on the spot. Then it has to grow back, which takes about a minute.
The Gun. Humans only, two bullets. It kills whoever it's played on, human or zombie. Every shot is announced, but never the target's role.
The Cure. Play it on a zombie, and they become human again, but you spend thirty seconds in quarantine. Play it on a human, and it's wasted. Holding it won't protect you.
Once per match, you can make a bluff call. Name the card your opponent is about to play. Get it right, and their card is cancelled, and you win. Get it wrong, and you lose ten points.
Once their Zombie card grows, a zombie has twenty seconds to use it, or they start starving: growling, and flaring green. Watch for faint green flickers, twitches, and glowing footprints.
Suspicious? Hit the emergency button in the central hall. The clock stops. Thirty seconds to talk, fifteen to vote. The most votes goes to quarantine. And remember: anyone can lie.
Found a body? Report it. That calls a meeting, without using your emergency button.

Humans have a second way to win. Four generator parts are hidden around the building. Pick one up, carry it down to the generator in the reactor, and fit it. Everyone can see who is carrying a part. And a zombie can grab one, and hide it.
Fit all four, and the power comes back. Ninety seconds later, the evac truck reaches the entrance. If more humans than zombies are standing inside, the humans escape, and win.
Zombies have a sabotage. Once per match, a zombie at the breaker in the server room can cut the lights. For fifteen seconds, humans can barely see. Zombies see just fine.
In the lobby, the security cameras show the last five room entries. Who went where, and how long ago.
When only one human is left, it's their last stand. They get a Gun with one bullet, and for five seconds, every zombie glows red.
Every ninety seconds, lightning lights up every room for a moment. Use emotes to point out a suspect. And when you're out, you walk on as a ghost, and keep watching.
Humans win by clearing out every zombie, or by escaping in the evac truck. Zombies win when no human is left. When time runs out, the bigger team wins, and a tie goes to the humans.

Your team wins or loses together. But your secret score decides who's the top player. The cards in your hand count: a number is worth its value, a Gun ten per bullet, a Cure thirty. Shoot a zombie, plus forty. Shoot a human, minus twenty. A bite, plus fifteen. Using your Cure costs its thirty, and wasting it on a human costs forty. And every full minute in your role adds ten.

Smart play earns more. Win a number duel, plus five. Fit a part, plus ten. A vote that helps your team, plus twenty. A zombie who is never accused, plus twenty-five. Survive your last stand, plus fifty.
After the match, read the full recap, earn experience, rank up, collect badges, and unlock new neon colours. And try the daily modifier, for a different night every day.
Outbreak Deck. Six to fifteen players. Five to eight minutes. Trust no one. And get to the evac.
